To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
floral resources have a positive effect on the longevity of a lacewing predator and a parasitoid of the predator, but that the effects of the resources depend on aphid prey density.

(i) the presence of flowers can have a positive effect on the density of lacewing larvae, but only at low prey (aphid, Acyrthosiphon pisum) density and (ii) the effect of floral nectar on the density of the lacewing larvae depends on the density of its parasitoid, Anacharis zeelandica (Hymenoptera: Figitidae), and the presence of floral nectar increases the longevity of adult parasitoids.
the effect of buckweat on lacewing ovoposition depends on aphid density and that the effect of the presence of buckweat in field cages on lacewing density is positive when aphid density is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the availability of floral resources and prey affects an omnivore and its parasitoids.
the role of floral resources for the regulation of a four trophi level system, which comprises a parasitoid, an omnivorous predator, aphids and alfalf.
understanding the impact of omnivory on multitrophic interactions and the role of floral resources for the regulation of herbivore populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of floral resources in a system can affect the interactions among species operating at different trophic levels.
the presence of floral resources may have a complex effect on a multitrophic system and may not necessarily be beneficial for all trophic levels.
buckwheat flowers are beneficial for the parasitoid and the lacewing, but not for the aphid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of buck wheat flowers in a field cage with pea aphids and their natural enemies, lacewing larvae and parasitoids, can have positive and negative effects on the lacewing larvae.
omnivores can have complex effects on higher trophic levels.
the effect of buckweat flowers on the lacewing population depends on the availability of aphids and the presence of the lacewing's parasitoid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
floral resources can have a strong effect on the dynamics of higher trophic levels, even though they may not directly affect the density of the target pest species.
omnivory and the presence of alternative resources for the top predators in a system have a substantial influence on the functioning of a four trophi level food web.

omnivores are important components of multitrophic interactions, and their role in food webs needs to be considered in order to fully understand the consequences of providing floral resources in agricultural systems.
